threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still get confused at which way to stand on the escalators during a tube strike. Locals just glide past you like it's second nature.
Last night on the 333, I saw a guy sing an entire Adele song to a bemused elderly couple. They turned their heads like it was a concert, proper London moment.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of grilled kebabs mixed with fresh coffee on any Saturday morning made me realize this is home, not just a place to live.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find nightclub briefs mixed with art exhibits in abandoned buildings—like a concert in a leftover factory, all while sipping on craft beer.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local when they know how to navigate the BART delays without losing their cool—or when they’ve got a backup plan that doesn’t involve Uber.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a glimpse of a guy in a tuxedo waiting for the N-Judah, holding a bouquet. Only in the Tenderloin would a wedding seem like it could happen on the subway.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always miss the tiny plaça on Carrer de Fraternitat where locals gather for evening chess. It’s a real slice of life, not a postcard spot.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by their confusion at the lack of pedestrian crossings; they’ll stand staring at the traffic, waiting for a green light.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still check the TfL app before hopping on the bus—locals know half the time it’s quicker to just walk.
Caught a night bus from Brixton; two drummers arguing about rhythms turned into a spontaneous jam session. Whole bus was vibing!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy in a full suit chatting with a busker while waiting for the tram—only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you enjoy a late-night döner with live saxophone on the corner—just another Wednesday vibe that feels so uniquely Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their quiet disdain for tourists trying to take photos in front of the taco trucks at midnight. Total vibe killer.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy playing the harp on the 31-Balboa, totally drowned out by the bus's screeching brakes. Classic Muni moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think all the bars here close at 2 AM, but locals know it’s not uncommon to find a few hidden spots open well into the sunrise.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they still reference 'el metro' when everyone just says 'el metro' without the article. Little things like that give them away.
